_comment: Row-major hold-ground reform on rally. A ROW-MAJOR player infantry block (60 men at 11 files -- five full ranks plus a centred 5-man rear rank -- with file_major_reform false) is staged already routing, with the enemy still a long way off. Staged that way deliberately: a rout that happens IN contact gets pinned by enemy soldier-body pressure and ground down rather than pulling clear, so it shatters instead of rallying -- rout-rally-recover.json and last-unit-rally.json are both that case. Here nothing is inside the rally-contact radius, so its morale climbs back toward the rout baseline and it re-forms where it stands, between ticks 180 and 240 on the 60 Hz state-dump basis. It rallies at tick 200 at nearly its full flee pace, so it first pulls up over about 65 wu (y~549 at the rally to 482) with its men braking in step, and stands near y=482 from about tick 320. The flee turn is a 180 from its spawn facing, so _face_dir's snap-absorb folds _formation_angle to PI and the rally's reform_ranks(hold_ground = true) takes the about-face branch: the depth reflection that re-squares the grid. Under the old raw index-order assignment that relabelled the whole block, so all 60 men walked the block's depth through the oncoming half to reach slots other men were vacating in the same tick. With the slot pairing only the six men whose rank has no same-width counterpart across the reflection have anywhere to go, and they hold their file and swap ends. A second, safe player unit well out of the rout-shock radius keeps the battle from declaring defeat while the infantry is routing. The router spawns at morale 22 rather than 5: a router now flees at its real flee pace, so the later rally the old staging gave carried the block off this camera and past the far-tier demotion range before it could re-form.

overlap.reason: Six unpaired soldiers in the incomplete rear rank swap ends across stationary ranks during post-rally hold-ground reform; the rally is at about tick 200 and the closest body pair is under the 2.25 wu floor from tick 244 to tick 304 on 2-tick samples (worst 0.31 wu at tick 266), against a worst of 0.07 wu on main 1f4a77eb, where the anchor stopped dead on the rally. Tracked in #1772.
